transcript.text: Thanks for joining this planning huddle. As you both know, the operations team and employee-support team currently hold separate weekly forums on the same afternoon, and employees have flagged that the agendas overlap. I have the authority to replace those two forums with a single recurring format and set its operating rules. Before I make anything binding, I want to hear from both of you about the practical constraints we need to account for — timing, format, capacity, anything that could make or break a combined forum. Let's start with the forum coordinator: what do we need to watch out for?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: There's a practical constraint I should put on the table: the employee-support forum currently includes confidential escalation cases that cannot be discussed in an open combined meeting. I've been handling those in a separate private portion of the existing forum. If we move to a single combined format, we need to make sure there's still a protected channel for those cases.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to raise a scheduling constraint on behalf of the remote employees I represent. Several of them have recurring morning caregiving responsibilities and cannot reliably join before 11:00. They can participate live by video at 11:00, and when an individual can't attend, they need a recorded summary. I haven't brought this to Helena before now, but it's critical that the combined forum doesn't start before 11:00 or these employees would be effectively shut out.

transcript.text: Thank you both — these are exactly the kinds of constraints I needed to hear before deciding. Omar, I understand we must preserve a protected channel for confidential escalation cases; a combined open forum cannot replace that. Tessa, I hear you that 11:00 is the earliest workable start time for remote employees with caregiving responsibilities, and recorded summaries are needed for those who still can't attend live. Before I settle on a format, let me ask one follow-up to each of you: Omar, can the confidential portion be handled as a separate private session immediately following the open combined forum, or does it need to be on a different day entirely? And Tessa, would 11:00 as a start time work for the combined forum, or is there a preference for slightly later to give a buffer?

transcript.text: Helena, a separate private session immediately following the open combined forum would work well. The confidential escalation cases don't need a different day — what matters is that they're handled in a closed session with only the relevant participants, not in the open combined portion. Keeping it right after the combined forum on the same afternoon would actually be efficient, since the context from the open discussion would still be fresh and we wouldn't need to schedule a second meeting window. As long as the operating rules clearly designate that portion as restricted-access, the constraint is satisfied.

The key requirements on my end are that the forum starts no earlier than 11:00 and that a recorded summary is available for anyone who still can't attend live. If both of those are built into the operating rules, the scheduling constraint is satisfied.

decisions.forum_structure: Single combined open forum replacing the two separate weekly forums, followed immediately by a separate private closed session for confidential escalation cases with restricted access limited to relevant participants only.
decisions.remote_participation_method: Live video participation at 11:00, with recorded summaries available for any remote employee who cannot attend live.

commitments.detail: The combined forum operating rules will clearly designate the post-forum private session as restricted-access, limited to relevant participants only, for handling confidential escalation cases.
The combined forum will start no earlier than 11:00 and recorded summaries will be produced and made available for any remote employee unable to attend live.
